{{Quote|Four Jedi&mdash;Masters Ludwin Katarkus and Everen Ettene plus their Padawans Danyawarra and Halagad Ventor&mdash;left Coruscant last month to try to settle the two-year old conflict between the Virgillian Free Alignment and the Aristocracy.|[[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] report|<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|jediwatch/13228_1.html|Virgillian Jedi Envoy Declared Lost}}</ref>}}
The '''Virgillia system''', also known as the '''Virgillian system''' or as '''Virgillian space''', was located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Koradin sector/Legends|Koradin sector]]. It contained the [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] [[Virgillia]] and [[Virgillia 7]]. The [[Star system/Legends|star system]] was the site of a [[Virgillian Civil War|civil war]] between the [[Aristocracy]] and the [[Virgillian Free Alignment/Legends|Virgillian Free Alignment]], which began during the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and continued in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]]. During the war, the Aristocracy controlled the Virgillia system and kept the Free Alignment confined to its [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] planets. The conflict eventually became a proxy war between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] once the Alliance began supporting the Free Alignment. The Free Alignment ultimately won, after which a truce between the two sides was established and the [[Virgillian Council]] was created to govern the system.

==Description==
The Virgillia [[Star system/Legends|system]], also known as the Virgillian system or Virgillian space,<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> was located in the [[Koradin sector/Legends|Koradin sector]]<ref name="Online Companion" /> of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was connected to the [[Lipsec system/Legends|Lipsec]] and [[Sump system/Legends|Sump systems]] by the [[Lipsec Run/Legends|Lipsec Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]]<ref name="Atlas" /> and contained the small terrestrial [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Virgillia 7]] as well as the planet [[Virgillia]] and its [[Virgillia's forested moon|forested moon]].<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" />

==History==
===Galactic Republic===
{{Quote|The Jedi diplomatic envoy dispatched to broker peace talks in the Virgillian Civil War has been declared lost after having been missing for three standard weeks.|HoloNet News report|<ref name="HNN" />}}
[[File:Javin_Oversector.jpg|thumb|right|300px|During the Clone Wars, the Virgillia system was located in the area of operations of the Galactic Republic's Nineteenth Sector Army.]]
The area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] surrounding the Virgillia system was [[Scout/Legends|explored]] between [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] and [[3000 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas" /> In [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]],<ref name="HNN date 23">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|jediwatch/13228_1.html|Virgillian Jedi Envoy Declared Lost}} is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] "13:2:28," which corresponds to [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]]. The [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 45|''HoloNet News Vol. 531 #45'']] [[HoloNet News/Legends|news]] story also establishes that the [[Virgillian Civil War]] began two [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior, thereby placing it in [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]].</ref> the [[Virgillian Civil War]] broke out in the [[Star/Legends|star]] system between the [[Aristocracy]], who controlled the system, and the [[Virgillian Free Alignment/Legends|Virgillian Free Alignment]].<ref name="HNN" /> During the war, the Aristocracy controlled all [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] technology in the system, forcing the Free Alignment to rely only on primitive [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]] such as [[Virgillian wheel lock|flintlocks]], and kept the Free Alignment confined to the system's colony worlds.<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" />

[[23 BBY/Legends|Two years]] later, a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] envoy was [[Mission to Virgillia 7|sent]]<ref name="HNN" /> to Virgillia 7<ref name="Skyewalkers">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref> to negotiate peace but was attacked upon arrival.<ref name="HNN" /> [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ashka Boda]], Galactic Republic [[Senator/Legends|senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]], and [[Gunslinger/Legends|gunslinger]] [[Giles Durane]] traveled to the Virgillia system shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]]<ref name="Skyewalkers" /> of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> in order to rescue the envoy's survivors.<ref name="Skyewalkers" />

The Virgillia system came to be situated in the territory in which, during the early campaigns of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the Republic's [[Nineteenth Army|Nineteenth Sector Army]] was tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="TEGtW" /> Shortly after the acquisition of the planet [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]] by the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] during that conflict, the Virgillia system was featured on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Map/Legends|map]] displayed on a [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]] at a facility run by [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]], the [[Magistrate/Legends|Magistrate]]<ref name="AoI">''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]''</ref> of the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]].<ref name="DB Argente">{{DB|character|passelargente|Argente, Passel}}</ref>

===End of the civil war and later history===
In the wake of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Declaration of a New Order|fall]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="TEGtW" /> the Aristocracy aligned itself with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> the Republic's successor.<ref name="TEGtW" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Virgillian Civil War was turned into a proxy war when the Free Alignment gained the support of the Empire's enemy, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. The Alliance provided the Free Alignment with [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and weaponry as well as tactical advice; the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] Rebel [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]] [[Monnda Tebbo]] was sent to the Virgillia system along with the [[Quasar Fire-class cruiser-carrier/Legends|''Quasar Fire''-class bulk cruiser]] ''[[Flurry]]'' as a navigation and [[Space warfare/Legends|space warfare]] instructor. [[Gender/Legends|He]] played such a significant role in the system's conflict that he was declared an honorary [[Virgillian]] citizen.<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" />

[[File:NagaiKodaVirgilliaMephout-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|In 4 ABY, the Nagai carried out an attack on the Virgillia system.]]
The Aristocracy also used Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] in its fight against the Virgillian Free Alignment. During the war, a small Imperial [[Fleet/Legends|armada]] that included the [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Stormwind]]'' under the [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jarroth]] patrolled the Virgillia system. While looking for Free Alignment activity, the ''Stormwind'' received information about a suspected Free Alignment encampment on Virgillia's forested moon from an Imperial informant in the system and traveled there to investigate. Despite the site turning out to be merely a [[Unidentified refugee camp|refugee camp]], stormtroopers [[Death/Legends|killed]] all of its inhabitants after [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] several for information.<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" />

As the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-wide war between the Empire and the Alliance intensified, the Imperial presence in the Virgillia system ended. Shortly before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Atlas" /> the war was finally won by the Free Alignment, after which an uneasy truce was established between the two opposing sides of the conflict and the [[Virgillian Council]] was created, becoming the system's new government.<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" />

Following the Free Alignment victory, the Virgillian Council dispatched two [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]]-[[Carrier/Legends|carriers]] of the [[Virgillian Free Alignment Starfleet|Starfleet]] to the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]], where the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] was rendezvousing for the upcoming confrontation in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], in order to join the Alliance's attack on the Empire's [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] [[Death Star/Legends|superweapon]] at Endor. The Virgillian ships subsequently also participated in an [[Bakura Incident|Alliance operation]] in the [[Bakura system/Legends|Bakura system]]. Another one of the Alignment's cruiser-carriers remained in the Virgillia system to defend against possible retaliatory Imperial attacks.<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> Later in 4 ABY,<ref name="Atlas" /> the [[Firefist|extragalactic]] [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] raiders [[Attack on Virgillia 7|attacked]] Virgillia 7, targeting its government, which by that [[Time/Legends|time]] had not yet aligned itself with the Rebel Alliance's successor, the [[Alliance of Free Planets]].<ref name="Forgotten War">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/nagai11202009/index.html|text=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs|int=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs}}</ref>

==Inhabitants==
The inhabitants of the Virgillia system were known as the Virgillians and almost entirely consisted of [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> Around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the system numbered between ten and one hundred million.<ref name="Atlas" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Readers who trace placements from the appendix back to the original sources will find some other implied tales here. For instance, there are a lot of battles, Imperial suppressions and Rebel struggles out around Virgillia and near Mon Calamari.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>}}
[[File:TruceBakura_Sourcebook.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Virgillia system was introduced in ''The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook''.]]
The Virgillia system was first mentioned in ''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]'', a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying guide]] published in [[1996]] by [[West End Games]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The book was written by [[Kathy Tyers]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]].<ref name="Bakura Sourcebook" /> The system's first [[in-universe]] appearance was on a galactic map in ''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]'', a [[Star Wars comic books|webcomic]] authored by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="AoI" /> over the span of the [[2009]]<ref name="AoI announcement">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20091001comics/index.html|text=New ''Clone Wars'' Web Comic Tells Original Tale}}</ref>&ndash;[[2010]]<ref name="Lethal Trackdown Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode222.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lethal Trackdown}}</ref> [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series.<ref name="AoI announcement" />

[[Jason Fry]],<ref name="Blog" /> co-author of the 2009 reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' that placed the Virgillia system in grid square I-18,<ref name="Atlas" /> noted in his endnotes for the book that the relative sparsity of the star system placement near the Virgillia system helped the readers of the work acquire a sense of the Outer Rim Territories' population distribution as well as that of the boundaries of "civilized" space. He also remarked that ''The Essential Atlas'' placed&mdash;via references in star system names&mdash;many "battles, Imperial suppressions and Rebel struggles" near the Virgillia system, which he hoped implied numerous potential story ideas that other ''[[Star Wars]]'' authors could use in future works.<ref name="Blog" />
